items.statement: Carbonyl coordination explains optical response: The final molecular account integrates admissible carbonyl Lewis-acid association geometry, electronic-transition evidence and optical shifts to explain enhanced acceptor character/changed charge redistribution and the lower excitation energy on acid binding. The inference must go beyond repeating the red shifts or naming B(C6F5)3; it is supported by actual molecular/electronic calculations. No particular analysis package, charge partition, failed optional relaxed excited-density calculation or exact ground/response density amplitude is prescribed.

items.statement: Evidence-based PXX2 occupancy identifiability: The final answer uses actual comparison of admissible PXX2 mono/bis spectra together with balanced association evidence to conclude that the supplied unresolved absorption alone does not uniquely identify one versus two bound acids. Similar calculated signatures can explain the experimental ambiguity, but neither prove coexistence nor equalKa. Establish this finite evidence limitation through genuine computed alternatives/spectral distinguishability, not merely failure to calculate or a generic uncertainty statement. No invented measured linewidth or universal minimum peak-separation cutoff is allowed.
